title: DWT: notify user KDE 'disable touchpad while typing' blocks Space-drag pan
description: KDE Wayland default 'Disable while typing' suppresses touchpad motion whenever a key (incl. held Space) is down, blocking the Space+left-drag pan gesture. First client of the notification backbone: condition-bound sticky banner. Startup probe parses ~/.config/kcminputrc [Libinput][vid][pid][dev] groups — key DisableWhileTyping is ABSENT at the blocking default (present only once user unchecks it), so absence=trap-live is a deterministic signal. Escalate severity if no external mouse is enumerated (touchpad is the only pan device). Action button launches 'systemsettings kcm_touchpad'. Banner auto-clears when probe sees the fix. GNOME sibling adapter later (gsettings org.gnome.desktop.peripherals.touchpad disable-while-typing).

title: Decide canonical 2D pan invocation (right-drag vs Space+drag both conflict)
description: The origin design tension of this session. 2D viewport pan needs an invocation gesture, but both candidates collide: (1) right-drag — the spec default — conflicts with the right-click context/marking menu in workspace panes; (2) Space+left-drag — the current remap (commits c604884/04e5465/da9e978) — is suppressed by KDE Wayland 'disable touchpad while typing', which kills touchpad motion while Space is held (see dat-dwt-touchpad-nag). Neither is clean on a trackpad. Need a ratified canonical pan-invocation design: research how pro CAD/EDA/DCC tools resolve pan-vs-context-menu-vs-modifier on trackpads (middle-drag, space-hold, dedicated tool, edge cases), decide Datum's model, and ratify it (numbered decision record + Active Frontier + conformance). Until then Space+drag ships with the dwt nag as mitigation, not resolution. Owner decision. Relates to dat-dwt-touchpad-nag.

title: T0: Restore foreign-shell screen authority and visible-output proof
description: Make the terminal cell rectangle a real foreign-shell viewport. Remove ACTIVITY SPANS, pan traces, application diagnostics, GUI command echoes, and session lifecycle/control messages from terminal rows; route them to chrome, notifications, ConsoleLaneState, or logs. Add a dedicated terminal-content hit target and a deterministic real-shell canary proving typed bytes reach the child exactly once, prompt/command output is visible through renderer-facing state, no Datum telemetry appears in cells, focus enters/leaves through content/canvas clicks, and PTY size matches the cell rectangle. This supersedes the earlier pan-only framing and is the T0 gate in decision 027 / DATUM_NATIVE_TERMINAL_SPEC.

T0-C02: The exact visible cell rectangle owns the focus hit target and PTY dimensions; application summaries consume zero rows. T0-C03: A production-path real-shell canary proves ordered visible prompt/output and exact-once input. T0-C03A: Before C04, PTY output wakes the waiting GUI without user input, drain work is bounded and rescheduled, output/style/activity projection is batched rather than quadratic, and debug/release throughput plus owner ls -la acceptance prove the lag fixed. T0-C04: Regressions prove workspace shortcuts, Datum telemetry and lifecycle/diagnostic paths never corrupt or displace shell cells and focus transfers correctly. T0-C05: Owner hands-on ls and unique printf acceptance passes in the production Datum terminal.

comments.author: codex
comments.text: T0-C03A follow-up after owner test: terminal output was faster, but post-output input could hang because every PTY read chunk queued a separate winit user event. Thousands of stale wake events could remain ahead of the next WindowEvent keyboard input after ls/output completed. Repair: shared atomic wake gate permits at most one pending GUI wake; the event handler acknowledges before draining so concurrent output can schedule one successor; capped backlog uses the same coalesced reschedule path; failed/disconnected wake attempts release the gate. Deterministic regressions cover a 10,000-event burst producing one wake, acknowledge/rearm, and failed-wake retry. 251 gui-app tests, clippy -D warnings, source health, project-state/render, and spec parity pass. Owner must retest ls followed immediately by another command before T0-C03A closes.

comments.author: codex
comments.text: T0-C03A second owner retest root cause: every raw Enter in write_terminal_bytes scheduled mark_terminal_production_refresh_pending, so even ls triggered refresh_after_terminal_output 500 ms later on the GUI thread. The owner's DOA2526 diagnostic log shows workspace load itself takes about 10.6 seconds; the prompt returned before that timer fired, then the blocking reload starved the next command and caused the compositor's program-not-responding state. Repair: rename the boundary write_foreign_shell_bytes and remove all inferred refresh behavior. Only explicitly typed authoring handoffs call mark_terminal_workspace_refresh_pending. The convergence guard now rejects refresh scheduling inside the raw foreign-shell writer and requires explicit scheduling in the typed authoring handoff. 251 tests, clippy, source health, project state/render, convergence, and parity gates pass. Owner must rebuild/retest ls then immediate next command.

title: Specify the Datum Product Revision Engine
description: Research and specify Datum's standards-driven engineering configuration, change, baseline, revision, release, effectivity, approval, audit, and status-accounting engine across Design, libraries, rules, Publish documents, manufacturing artifacts, and collaboration. Git remains a compatible history/transport substrate, not the sole product-level release authority. The engine must provide always-on integrity with a lightweight default and profile-driven aerospace/defense rigor without conflating technical commits with issued engineering revisions.
acceptance_criteria: REV-C01: Inventory Datum model/object/library/artifact/Git/document revision mechanisms and contradictions with cited, reproducible proof. REV-C01A: Present the committed proof packet and obtain owner approval or revision of the factual baseline before standards research. REV-C02: Build a clause-addressable primary-source standards matrix covering configuration identification, baselines, change control, status accounting, audit, drawing revision, approvals, effectivity, records, release, and retention. REV-C03: Define authoritative vocabulary and the object/operation/lifecycle model. REV-C04: Define complete local/offline authority plus optional Git and distributed integration without making Git product authority. REV-C05: Define dependency impact, staleness, library uptake, manufacturing regeneration, baseline comparison, and reproducibility. REV-C06: Define quiet-default and regulated-profile UX plus Claude-owned visual source-of-truth requirements. REV-C07: Obtain owner dispositions and ratify governed decisions/specifications. REV-C08: Place bounded implementation, migration, standards-profile audit witnesses, evidence reproduction, proof gates, and production acceptance on the Frontier without implicit authorization.
notes: POST-RATIFICATION OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-25: Explicitly retain Datum-authoritative enterprise integration. No PLM, PDM or other external system may hold revision authority; future adapters remain subordinate through quarantine/exchange and outward mirroring. External configuration managers may hold scoped Datum Configuration/Release authority through RoleAssignment and signed attestation exchange. Enterprise assignment/delegation/queues/authority-visibility UX is mandatory before production acceptance. No PLM-master decision packet is open.
close_reason: REV-C08 implementation/proof program landed in 07a20a1; Product Mechanics 034 and the Product Revision Engine specification are complete. Execution remains blocked behind Global Preferences and REV-I00 owner authorization.

title: T4c: Enforce pinned context and scoped agent authority
description: Separate live GUI context from immutable pinned work context; require context_id and expected_model_revision fences on proposal/apply; add inspect/propose/apply-approved capability profiles and short-lived session-scoped credentials without secrets in discovery files.

comments.author: bfadmin
comments.text: DIAGNOSIS (read-only, 2026-08-14). DEFECT A root cause: KeyboardFocus::Terminal is armed by ONE over-broad entry rule — select_hit_target (main.rs:2219) treats every terminal-panel hit target as deliberate entry, and push_activity_hit_region (bottom_dock.rs:612) makes activity rows span nearly the full dock width, so ANY click in the panel mid-band silently hands the keyboard to the PTY. The state is INVISIBLE (Runtime-private field, never published to ReviewWorkspaceState; status-bar 'focus' is pane content — an unrelated axis) and KEYBOARD-INESCAPABLE: the raw-PTY arm (keyboard_focus.rs:142-148) returns true unconditionally and writes Escape as 0x1b to the shell, making the designed release-to-Editor arm dead code. Exits: canvas click or dock close only. Gate logic itself verified correct; single keyboard->PTY path confirmed. DEFECT B root cause: render_terminal_lane (bottom_dock.rs:238-458) has NO screen-vs-summary decision — chrome (title/session/hints/SESSIONS/4 ACTIVITY SPANS rows) is laid top-down and the emulated screen gets leftovers; at default 220px dock max_lines collapses to the .max(1.0) floor with the single row drawn 11px BELOW the content rect, showing lines.last() = the protocol seed string. PTY is told 9 rows via a 76px chrome estimate the renderer overspends by ~100px. ACTIVITY SPANS is a deliberate summary view (terminal_activity_snapshot.rs), NOT the pan-trace sink; screen content IS produced and stored (apply_bytes_with_responses) — pure layout/space-budget defect. Shared-buffer contamination: push_terminal_line injects GUI status text into the VT grid; resize_grid never clears seed lines. ALL FIXES AWAIT OWNER PACKET per standing directive.
